title: The command-substitution copy loop can still permanently take a worker
trigger: With one Tokio worker, run `value=$(<big.txt)` where `big.txt` is a regular text file larger than the substitution pipe's capacity—for example, 1 MiB.
measured: The copy keeps the worker until its synchronous pipe write blocks. The task that must drain that pipe cannot run. **The command and its timeout remain stuck, and later shell calls cannot be served.** This is an ordinary finite-file trigger, not just an endless builtin.
closed_evidence: The original `value=$(<big.txt)` completed with exit code **0** at both **1 MiB and 16 MiB** on one scheduler worker.
how_found_quote: No repository edits, branch changes, Rust builds, tests, or `bun check` runs. Findings above are source-derived, not runtime reproductions.

title: Expansion and glob traversal still monopolize a worker before the new checkpoint
trigger:
| File and lines | Exact trigger |
|---|---|
| `interp.rs:1405–1407`; `expansion.rs:647–665, 777–815` | `for i in {1..3000000}; do :; done` |
| `patterns.rs:465–508, 519–529` | `: huge-directory/*`, where the directory contains enough entries to outlast the command deadline |
| `patterns.rs:608–664` | `shopt -s globstar; : huge-tree/**/nonexistent`, over a large native directory tree |
measured: **User consequence:** If the deadline becomes ready while this work occupies the sole worker—or all workers are occupied by such work—the task that sets cancellation cannot run. Timeout/abort and unrelated shell work are delayed until expansion finishes. These finite workloads eventually release the worker; they are **not necessarily permanent wedges**, unlike finding 1.
closed_evidence: The glob and globstar finding is closed for the tested walk: cancellation of a 3,000-entry walk was observed in roughly **1–5 ms** on one worker.
how_found_quote: The glob paths retain the original ineffective pattern: `ensure_not_cancelled()` inside loops whose `.await`s stay ready on native filesystems. I followed those calls into `pi-vfs`: native `read_dir`, metadata and directory-entry type operations run synchronously, without yielding.

title: Nonmatching `case` branches retain an early-`continue` path with no checkpoint
trigger: Execute a generated `case hit in … esac` containing many nonmatching literal alternatives—for example, 100,000 repetitions of `miss) : ;;`—while a cancellation task becomes runnable during matching.
measured: **User consequence:** Cancellation and other work on that worker remain delayed until the scan ends. The inner pattern loop at line 1489 also needs coverage: one case arm with many `|`-separated alternatives bypasses even the outer cancellation check until all alternatives have been examined.
closed_evidence: A 100,000-**arm** `case` cancelled in **54 ms**; its alternatives-in-one-arm sibling above did not.
how_found_quote: Every unsuccessful case takes `continue` at line 1502, without executing a body and therefore without reaching a `CompoundList` checkpoint.

title: Cancelled copies retain blocking workers
trigger: On the gate VM, with one scheduler worker and a **two-thread blocking pool**, two `value=$(<idle_fifo)` runs timed out; a subsequent ordinary 1 MiB `value=$(<small)` also timed out, while `printf healthy` succeeded. Aborting a direct copy mid-read likewise left its sole blocking slot unavailable until I closed the pipe writer.
measured: On the gate VM, with one scheduler worker and a **two-thread blocking pool**, two `value=$(<idle_fifo)` runs timed out; a subsequent ordinary 1 MiB `value=$(<small)` also timed out, while `printf healthy` succeeded. Aborting a direct copy mid-read likewise left its sole blocking slot unavailable until I closed the pipe writer. The normal Windows Node-API runtime configures **eight** blocking threads in `pi-natives/src/lib.rs:103–108`: **[INFERENCE]** eight such occupied slots exhaust that pool, fewer if other work occupies slots. Linux uses the Tokio default rather than this eight-thread configuration.
closed_evidence: **The three original wedge reproducers are closed for their original causes.** The *unmodified*, bug-asserting probes printed `next_copy_starved=false`, `healthy_copy_timeout=false`, and `eval_pipeline_timeout=false`; their assertions therefore failed as expected.
how_found_quote: On the gate VM, with one scheduler worker and a **two-thread blocking pool**, two `value=$(<idle_fifo)` runs timed out

title: An ordinary nested substitution can deadlock a full pool without a FIFO
trigger: A non-async `eval` pipeline stage holds a blocking thread in `commands.rs:665–700`, then its substitution queues another blocking task at `openfiles.rs:310`. With a one-thread blocking pool, a standalone 1 MiB substitution succeeded, but `eval 'value=$(<small)' | /bin/cat` timed out; the next standalone substitution timed out too.
measured: With a one-thread blocking pool, a standalone 1 MiB substitution succeeded, but `eval 'value=$(<small)' | /bin/cat` timed out; the next standalone substitution timed out too. Unrelated `printf` still succeeded. This is pool exhaustion caused by the new offload itself, not a deliberately stalled input.
closed_evidence: The *unmodified*, bug-asserting probes printed `next_copy_starved=false`, `healthy_copy_timeout=false`, and `eval_pipeline_timeout=false`; their assertions therefore failed as expected.
how_found_quote: `eval 'value=$(<small)' | /bin/cat` timed out; the next standalone substitution timed out too.

title: “Source length” does not bound cancellation latency
trigger: With the script pre-parsed and cancellation ready before execution, a **989 KiB, generated `case` with 100,000 alternatives in one arm** ran for **5.42 s and returned success despite cancellation**.
measured: a **989 KiB, generated `case` with 100,000 alternatives in one arm** ran for **5.42 s and returned success despite cancellation**. ... A generated **one-million-element keyed array** (10.9 MB of source) likewise ignored cancellation for **1.78 s** through `interp.rs:2093–2116`. ... By contrast, 100,000 *plain* array elements and 100,000 simple-command arguments were cancelled in **11 ms** and **16 ms**
closed_evidence: **Expansion checkpoints:** the head stopped cancellations rather than ignoring them: 100,000 alternatives in one `case` arm **33.6 ms**; one million keyed literals **199 ms** after a separately measured 2.32 s parse
how_found_quote: ran for **5.42 s and returned success despite cancellation**

title: The synchronous expansion preface remains unbounded
trigger: A pre-parsed, **18-byte** `arr=({1..3000000})` took **1.09 s** to observe cancellation.
measured: A pre-parsed, **18-byte** `arr=({1..3000000})` took **1.09 s** to observe cancellation. This is substantially better than the reported old-head stall, but still a runtime-data-sized interval without a yield. I measured the brace path, not a separate large `split_fields` fixture.
closed_evidence: three-million-word brace range **0.324 ms**; and one 16 MiB field **7.69 ms**.

title: Mixed virtual/native copies no longer stream
trigger: In a paired gate-VM run copying a 256 MiB ready virtual source to an asynchronously drained native pipe.
measured: the old implementation delivered its first byte in **138 µs** with no measured rise above the process’s prior peak resident set; this head delivered it in **97 ms** and raised that peak by **124,780 KiB**. Thus the comment that whole-copy buffering “costs nothing extra” is not borne out.
closed_evidence: The independent 256 MiB streaming probe measured first byte **100.5 ms → 131.8 µs** and peak resident-set-size *increase* **230,692 KiB → no measured increase**.
how_found_quote: the old implementation delivered its first byte in **138 µs** ... this head delivered it in **97 ms** and raised that peak by **124,780 KiB**

title: A stream without a borrowable descriptor wedges the Tokio worker
trigger: `CopySide::classify` sends a permitted `OpenFile::Stream` whose `try_borrow_as_fd` fails to synchronous `Plain` I/O. With one worker, a pipe-backed stream held that worker until an external rescue at 500.5 ms; its writer task scheduled for 100 ms never ran.
measured: With one worker, a pipe-backed stream held that worker until an external rescue at 500.5 ms; its writer task scheduled for 100 ms never ran. The identical VM probe on `16707e14f352` finished in 101.7 ms, with the writer task running. **[INFERENCE]** Without the rescue writer, the new worker remains parked. This reintroduces the original class of wedge.
how_found_quote: a pipe-backed stream held that worker until an external rescue at 500.5 ms; its writer task scheduled for 100 ms never ran

title: Restoring shared descriptor flags can wedge another active copy
trigger: On the VM, aborting the first copy changed the shared flags from nonblocking back to blocking while the second was pending.
measured: On the VM, aborting the first copy changed the shared flags from nonblocking back to blocking while the second was pending. A 40 ms heartbeat did not run until a separate writer supplied data at **400.3 ms**. This is not solved by having a reactor registration: its subsequent raw read can block.
how_found_quote: aborting the first copy changed the shared flags from nonblocking back to blocking while the second was pending

title: Raw syscalls bypass the `OpenFile` read/write contract and lose data
trigger: Three old-head → new-head VM comparisons: after buffered `stdin.read_line()` consumed `one\n`, copying stdin; a descriptor-backed `Stream` that reads `prefix-` before its pipe; a descriptor-backed `Stream` that uppercases writes.
measured:
- After buffered `stdin.read_line()` consumed `one\n`, copying stdin returned the buffered `two\n` on the old head but **empty output** on this head.
- A descriptor-backed `Stream` that reads `prefix-` before its pipe returned `prefix-tail` before and **`tail`** now.
- A descriptor-backed `Stream` that uppercases writes produced `HELLO` before and **`hello`** now.
how_found_quote: The polled path calls `libc::read` and `libc::write`, not `OpenFile`’s `Read`/`Write` implementations. Three old-head → new-head VM comparisons:

title: `O_NONBLOCK` is visible to the shell’s caller, including after aborting a shell run
trigger: In a VM shell probe, stdin flags went `0x0 → 0x800` and remained `0x800` after the parent run was aborted.
measured: In a VM shell probe, stdin flags went `0x0 → 0x800` and remained `0x800` after the parent run was aborted. A concurrent `/bin/cat` exited **1**, reporting `Resource temporarily unavailable`; on the old head flags remained `0x0` and `cat` exited **0**. Flags returned to `0x0` only after the writer closed. Two copies using the same process-stdin descriptor also made one copy fail with `WouldBlock` on the new head; both completed on the old head. A user-supplied duplicated fd has the same shared-flag exposure.
how_found_quote: In a VM shell probe, stdin flags went `0x0 → 0x800` and remained `0x800` after the parent run was aborted. A concurrent `/bin/cat` exited **1**, reporting `Resource temporarily unavailable`

title: The ruled array-construction residual is not bounded by 138 ms
trigger: In a real shell run, cancellation requested just after the last expansion of `big=("${seed[@]}" "$trigger")`.
measured: cancellation requested just after the last expansion of `big=("${seed[@]}" "$trigger")` took **1.455 s** to return; the shell had already assigned **3,000,001 elements**. Directly exercising `ShellValue::indexed_array_from_literals` took 1.612 s for 3 million elements and 5.687 s for 10 million, with cancellation waiting 1.601 s and 5.677 s respectively. Separately, cancellation during `element_values`’ synchronous clone overshot **263 ms** at 3 million elements.
how_found_quote: took **1.455 s** to return; the shell had already assigned **3,000,001 elements**

title: Registration panic permanently changes a shared fd
trigger: `PolledFd::new` sets `O_NONBLOCK` *before* `AsyncFd::new`. On a Tokio runtime with I/O disabled, registration panicked; no `PolledFd` existed to run its `Drop`.
measured: On a Tokio runtime with I/O disabled, registration panicked; no `PolledFd` existed to run its `Drop`, and the retained pipe’s flags stayed **`0x0 → 0x800`**. The same old-head probe returned without panic and kept `0x0`. A panic **during** a copy whose `PolledFd` had already been constructed *did* restore flags; the gap is construction-time unwinding.
how_found_quote: On a Tokio runtime with I/O disabled, registration panicked; no `PolledFd` existed to run its `Drop`, and the retained pipe’s flags stayed **`0x0 → 0x800`**.

title: A caller checkpoint does not cover all work inside one expansion element
trigger: One `"${seed[@]}"` piece can supply three million fields to that single call. In VM cancellation sweeps of `copy=("${seed[@]}")`, requests at 100–3,000 ms.
measured: In VM cancellation sweeps of `copy=("${seed[@]}")`, requests at 100–3,000 ms overshot by **49–198 ms**; one at 4,000 ms overshot **722 ms** and assigned the full array. Those timings **do not isolate coalescing from array construction**; the source establishes that coalescing itself has no checkpoint.
how_found_quote: requests at 100–3,000 ms overshot by **49–198 ms**; one at 4,000 ms overshot **722 ms** and assigned the full array
